question.text: Sahyadri Stat-Arb Fund (Cat III AIF) earns the bulk of its returns from index futures and options. Under Chapter 14 of the workbook, how is such F&O income characterised for the fund?

answer.text: Capital gains (STCG) taxed at 20% under Section 111A
Profits and Gains from Business and Profession, taxable at MMR

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook explicitly: 'Any gains arising from these [F&O] transactions shall be treated as Profits and Gains from Business and Profession and the fund should be liable to pay tax on such income at the MMR of Tax, i.e. 42.744%.' Derivatives are NOT capital assets for a trading fund. The Trap: Candidates may force STCG/LTCG framing (A/B) because F&O positions are short-duration — but the character is business income, not capital gains. D is the Cat I/II pass-through exemption, inapplicable to Cat III. Cross-Exam Context: VIII (Equity Derivatives) treats F&O at retail level as speculation/business. XIX-E drills the fund-level classification because MMR attaches. XIX-D (Cat I/II) would not normally hit this — Cat I/II AIFs are PE/VC and seldom heavy F&O users. Manager's Pro-Tip: At Sahyadri, the F&O MMR character means set-off options are narrower — F&O loss is business loss (non-speculative), set-off-able against any business head but NOT capital gains. Book trading-loss carve-outs carefully because speculation-vs-derivative classification has bite on carry-forward duration (8 yrs non-spec vs 4 yrs spec).
